policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the phrase adjectivally as 'a deadly arrow', with no ASV note attached to this unit. 'Deadly' shows neither the passive voice of the qere participle shachut nor the active voice of the ketiv shochet; an arrow called deadly is equally one that slays (ketiv) and one that is sharpened/slaughtering-made (qere). No italicized supply and no other ASV wording in 9:8 bears on the participle's form, so the English permits both readings and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
